message:
Please review the following document.

<document>
**Note on the request amount:** I wrote this summary as a **$220,000** request, not $250,000. The Foundation caps capital at 40% of the award, so a $250,000 grant could put at most $100,000 toward the $165,000 truck. The only other costs you listed are $120,000 a year in operating costs. That makes $220,000 the most this budget can justify. To ask for $250,000, you would need $30,000 in additional eligible first-year costs that aren't in the figures you gave me. Bracketed items are facts I don't have and shouldn't invent.

---

# Grant Summary: Rural Mobile Pantry Expansion
**Harvest Table Food Bank | Request: $220,000 (one year) | Total project cost: $285,000**

## The need
Demand for food assistance in our county is rising quickly. Harvest Table served 18,200 households in 2025, up 26% from 14,450 in 2023. The gap is widest in Hollis, Wren and Tamarack townships, where food insecurity is estimated at 17%, compared with 11% countywide.

Supply is also tightening. The county's federal TEFAP commodity allocation, about 30% of our inventory, will be cut by 18% in fiscal year 2027. That is a loss of roughly 5% of our total food supply. We plan to replace it through [food sourcing plan].

## The project
Our mobile pantry currently runs two refrigerated trucks to nine rural sites each month. This project adds:
- a third refrigerated truck,
- a full-time driver and a site coordinator, and
- six new monthly distribution sites in the three highest-need townships.

Each visit provides about 42 pounds of food per household, including fresh and refrigerated items. In year one we expect to serve [number] households and distribute [number] pounds.

## Sites and schedule
The county Department of Social Services will host all six sites in its field-office parking lots at no cost. This lets us launch quickly and connects clients to DSS services on site. However, DSS lots are available only on weekdays from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. In our survey of rural clients, 58% work hourly jobs, and most prefer evening or Saturday distributions. During year one we will:
- recruit evening and Saturday host sites in each township [named prospects, if any], and
- track attendance by time slot so the schedule follows client needs.

## Cost-effectiveness
Mobile distribution costs $0.61 per pound, compared with $0.19 through our 61 volunteer-run partner pantries. That works out to about $26 per household visit. We use the mobile model only where volunteer pantries cannot reach people.

We hold the existing program to the same standard. Attendance has fallen at four of our nine current sites. We are reviewing each one and will consolidate or relocate sites that no longer meet need.

## Budget

| Item | Total | Carlisle request |
|---|---|---|
| Refrigerated truck (one-time) | $165,000 | $100,000 (40% of award) |
| Driver and site coordinator | $92,000 | $92,000 |
| Fuel and maintenance | $28,000 | $28,000 |
| **Total** | **$285,000** | **$220,000** |

The remaining $65,000 for the truck will come from [source and whether it is committed].

A local grocery chain will donate the truck's branding wrap and $15,000 a year in grocery gift cards for clients.

## Sustainability
After the grant year, the program will need $120,000 a year to continue. We will fund it through [specific sources, amounts and status]. Harvest Table has a $3.4 million operating budget and ended 2025 with a $40,000 surplus.

## Measuring results
We will report on:
- households served,
- pounds distributed,
- attendance by site and time slot, and
- cost per pound,

and share findings with the Foundation at six and twelve months.

---

#

response:
# Review: Rural Mobile Pantry Expansion Grant Summary

## The $220,000 request breaks the 40% capital cap

The table puts $100,000 toward the truck and calls it "40% of award." But $100,000 is 40% of **$250,000**. On a $220,000 award, it's **45.5%**.

Solving for the largest compliant award, where operating costs are $120,000 and capital is at most 40% of the award:

- Award = capital + $120,000, and capital ≤ 0.4 × award
- So 0.6 × award ≤ $120,000, which gives **award ≤ $200,000** (with **$80,000** for the truck)

The note's reasoning about $250,000 is correct: that award would need $150,000 in eligible non-capital costs, or $30,000 more than you have. The error is the claim that $220,000 is the most the budget can justify. It's $200,000.

**Corrected budget:**

| Item | Total | Carlisle request |
|---|---|---|
| Refrigerated truck (one-time) | $165,000 | $80,000 (40% of award) |
| Driver and site coordinator | $92,000 | $92,000 |
| Fuel and maintenance | $28,000 | $28,000 |
| **Total** | **$285,000** | **$200,000** |

These changes follow from the correction:
- The header request becomes **$200,000**.
- The truck gap becomes **$85,000**, not $65,000.
- In the note, the $220,000 figures become $200,000. The $30,000 explanation for reaching $250,000 can stay as written.

Please confirm whether the cap applies to the award or to total project cost. If it applies to project cost, the math changes.

## Figures that check out

- Household growth: 14,450 to 18,200 is +25.95%, so "26%" is right.
- TEFAP: an 18% cut to 30% of inventory is 5.4%, so "roughly 5%" is right.
- Cost per visit: $0.61 × 42 lb = $25.62, so "about $26" is right.

## Questions a reviewer is likely to ask

1. **Why buy a third truck while four of nine sites are declining?** The summary admits the falling attendance but doesn't connect it to the request. Explain why freeing up existing truck capacity can't cover some of the new townships. Or say that consolidation is already factored in.
2. **Why launch at sites with hours most clients can't use?** The summary says 58% of clients work hourly jobs and prefer evenings or Saturdays, then commits all six sites to weekday DSS hours. The candor helps, but add a target, such as "at least two evening or Saturday sites by month six." Otherwise it reads as building in a known access problem.
3. **The $40,000 surplus works against you.** Next to a $120,000 annual need, it covers only a third and invites the question of why the gap isn't funded already. Mention it only with the specific sustainability sources, or cut it.
4. **The grocery partnership goes unused.** The wrap and $15,000 a year in gift cards are real leverage but aren't counted anywhere. Consider showing them as in-kind contributions, or noting them under sustainability, since the gift cards recur.

## Placeholders and sourcing

- **Year-one targets:** As a rough check, $120,000 ÷ $0.61/lb ≈ 197,000 lb, or about 4,700 household visits. Across 72 distributions (6 sites × 12 months), that's about 65 households per stop. This holds only if the $0.61 rate covers costs similar to this budget, so verify it against your own data before using it.
- **Funding sources:** The truck match and post-grant sustainability placeholders are the most important to fill. Funders weigh committed versus pending money heavily.
- **Citations:** Cite sources for the 17% and 11% food-insecurity estimates (e.g., Map the Meal Gap) and the FY2027 TEFAP cut.
- **Personnel:** Confirm whether the $92,000 includes fringe benefits.

## Minor

- Delete the stray `#` at the end of the document.
- The Foundation is named ("Carlisle") only in the table header. Use the name in the text too, or use "Foundation request" in the table.
